headline: U.S. Bancorp has not encountered third-party AI cash-sorting agents
body: On the third-quarter call, CEO Gunjan Kedia said the bank has not encountered third-party AI cash-sorting agents. Kedia said the logistics are “very complicated” and that the bank does not expect a near-term impact. Average deposits increased 2.9% year over year.
note: Kedia pointed to the bank’s own digital tools for deposit pricing. He put outside cash-sorting agents beyond the near term.

evidence.text: U.S. Bancorp ’s consumers continued to spend during the third quarter, even as the bank carried more card balances and saw an increase in early-stage card delinquencies.
Asked whether personal AI agents could automatically move cash among banks to seek better rates, CEO Gunjan Kedia said U.S. Bank has not encountered third-party AI cash-sorting agents.
“The logistics of doing something like this are very complicated, so we do not expect it to be a near-term impact to us,” Kedia said.
Average deposits increased 2.9% year over year and 2.2% sequentially, with consumer deposits reaching another quarterly record.

U.S. Bank’s existing digital tools already provide deposit price discovery and automated optimization options, according to Kedia, who added that the technology is already being used internally for productivity.
